description: Screens framework objectives for applicability to a target service BEFORE mapping, using capability flags (service-capability-rules.json) and derived category labels (service-category-rules.json). Three rule kinds, each risk-averse: an objective is only marked N/A when there is a POSITIVE structural reason (an organizational/shared-responsibility objective, or a category fact that the service's category structurally lacks the capability). An UNKNOWN capability NEVER forces N/A — it defers to the objective's KB default (data/domain-mapping-guidance/<framework>.json). Objective IDs reference CCMv4. Consumed by scripts/compute-applicability-matrix.py.

semantics.intrinsic_na_rules: Objectives that no per-service platform/infrastructure control can satisfy for ANY service (physical datacenter, endpoint/HR, organizational governance). Always N/A. Independent of capabilities.
semantics.category_na_rules: Objectives that are N/A for services IN a given category, because that category structurally lacks the capability the objective needs (e.g. serverless_compute has no customer-managed OS to patch and no customer-managed backup API). Fires only when the service carries one of na_for_categories. A category fact, not a per-export absence.
semantics.capability_unlock_rules: Objectives the KB defaults to N/A that become applicable ONLY when a required capability is definitively PRESENT (e.g. a backup-capable service unlocks BCR-08). Present -> applicable (optionally capped by max_coverage). Absent/unknown -> no override (KB default stands). These never force N/A.

intrinsic_na_rules.reason: Physical and environmental datacenter security is managed by AWS under the shared-responsibility model; no customer-deployable service control satisfies these.
Endpoint/device management is an organizational IT domain; no AWS service control satisfies it.
Personnel/HR security controls are organizational processes; no technical service control satisfies them.
Audit and assurance objectives describe organizational governance programs; no platform/infrastructure configuration control implements them.

category_na_rules.reason: Serverless compute has no customer-managed operating system or runtime to patch or scan — AWS patches the execution environment. OS/software patching and vulnerability-metric objectives are N/A.
category_na_rules.capability_note: Fires on the category, NOT on any per-export mention of a runtime; a descriptive 'custom runtime' string in an entity information field must never assert customer patching.

category_na_rules.reason: Serverless compute exposes no customer-configurable backup, snapshot, or DR-exercise API; backup-verification and DR-exercise objectives are N/A. Multi-AZ placement is resilience, not backup.
Serverless compute owns no audit-log store to protect; the log store (CloudWatch Logs group, CloudTrail trail, S3 log bucket) is a separate service's resource. Log-store protection is N/A here.
category_na_rules.capability_note: A store-owning service in another category keeps LOG-02/LOG-09 mappable; this fires only on the serverless_compute category.

capability_unlock_rules.reason_when_present: Service exposes a customer-configurable backup/snapshot/replication API, so backup-verification and DR-exercise objectives are in scope.
